chunks: Whoever comes with good (deeds) will receive better than (what he had done), and be safe that day from terror.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for good deeds on the Day of Judgment according to Surah An-Naml?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to highlight the principle of *Hasanah* (good deed) yielding a multiplied reward, underscores the divine generosity where the reward exceeds the deed itself. It further assures the faithful of *Aman* (security) from the overwhelming terror (*Faza'*) that grips humanity on the Day of Resurrection, a theme frequently linked with the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet.
